transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-01-29
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~64 minutes
- Recording: internal link omitted
- Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Hank (Redwood SE), Jamal, Marta, Samir, Leah (Aurora)

Summary:
Quick postmortem-style deep dive on Aurora's private VPC deployment where you saw intermittent 120-350ms tail latency spikes when the Dedicated inference nodes were run through PrivateLink + NAT egress. We walked through networking, DNS behavior, MTU, KV cache cold starts, batching windows, and quantization/cold path interactions. Action items and a bench plan agreed.

Topics covered:
- PrivateLink connectivity and hairpin egress patterns
- NAT gateway / ephemeral port exhaustion and flow table TTLs
- VPC MTU mismatches across peered subnets and ENI attachment path
- DNS resolver timeouts and resolver chaining (AWS + on-prem resolvers)
- KV cache cold-start and prefix cache misses causing extra RPCs
- Batching windows vs latency SLOs and qbatch quantization tradeoffs
Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (AE): alright thanks everyone for hopping on, um we wanted to go through the run from last friday and try to triangulate whether this is primarily a network egress issue or something in the runtime, so i'll kick off, priya you wanna frame the observed symptoms?
[00:18] Priya (SE): yeah sure. so we saw consistent p50 around 18ms which is fine, but the tail was spiky - like 120 to 350ms intermittently on the same batch sizes. The interesting bit is that spikes correlated with certain source subnets that route via the nat/privatelink path into aurora's firewall, erm, firewall appliance.
[00:36] Jamal (Aurora): yea to add, we think it started after enabling cross-account PrivateLink to the redwood dedicated endpoint. We also observed a matching bump in nat gateway active connections and some retransmits.
[00:51] Marta (Aurora): and just to be clear, this was when we queued 16-way batching at 8 tokens avg payloads, so throughput was high, not small toy requests.
[01:08] Priya (SE): okay good, that helps - batching can amplify underlying network jitter if egress tails block the request path. One suspicion: hairpin egress where traffic from private subnets goes out to a nat and back in via PrivateLink loops, which can hit MTU mismatches.
[01:27] Leah (Aurora): we did see some ICMP fragmentation in the VPC flow logs but not consistent. we also have an on-prem resolver chained behind the nat for some services, maybe DNS is adding 50-100ms on retries.
[01:45] Hank (SE): quick question — are you running TLS termination on the appliance or is traffic end-to-end to our endpoint? if there's middlebox tls intercept that can add CPU queues.
[02:00] Samir (Security): we don't intercept TLS; appliance is L4, but we do have SNI inspection and some logging that can buffer connections when load is high.
[02:13] Priya (SE): alright, that narrows it. i want to walk through the timeline from client request to token return: client -> alb -> private subnet -> nat (egress) -> private link endpoint -> redwood dedicated ENI -> inference runtime. on return path the runtime does KV-cache lookups (if not hot) and might call to redis-like service or disk, adding to RTT.
[02:39] Alex (AE): can you show the nat metrics you pulled? Jamal, do you have the spike window?
[02:47] Jamal (Aurora): yep uploaded a csv. We saw transient port shortages, ephemeral port utilization hitting 65k ranges during big runs, plus a handful of tcp retransmit peaks. i'll paste the link in the notes.
[03:05] Marta (Aurora): also noticed a pattern where requests that triggered a quantized model fallback had worse tails — maybe the runtime was loading different kernels or quantized weights from disk.
[03:22] Priya (SE): that makes sense. When the runtime falls back to a different quantization path or reloads tensors we can see 20-80ms cold load plus extra GC/alloc time. Combine that with a network retry and you get compounded tail.
[03:38] Alex (AE): okay let's break into hypothesis buckets: 1) NAT/PrivateLink hairpin + MTU causes fragmentation and retransmits 2) DNS resolver retry chains adding latency 3) KV-cache cold miss / model quantization reload 4) appliance buffering on high connections. We should attempt to falsify each.
[03:58] Jamal (Aurora): quick note — the PrivateLink interface in our account is cross-account and uses interface ENIs across multiple AZs; we saw an AZ skew where us-east-1b had more spikes. could be route tables or ENI placement.
[04:15] Priya (SE): nice catch. AZ affinity can create asymmetric path lengths if your nat is in a different AZ than the PrivateLink ENI; that will increase cross-AZ traffic and NAT hops.
[04:33] Leah (Aurora): we also had an earlier change where MTU on one transit ENI was 1500 but the bridge over our on-prem VPN was 9001; maybe fragmentation happens only on certain path combos.
[04:48] Hank (SE): fragmentation at the VPN boundary can lead to TCP PMTUD issues; if PMTUD fails and Path MTU blackholes, you get retransmits and long timeouts.
[05:02] Alex (AE): can you run a traceroute with DF bit set during bench windows? that helps show where fragmentation occurs.
[05:11] Jamal (Aurora): will do.
[05:18] Priya (SE): another easy instrument: capture DNS timings. if resolver takes 100ms to time out then requests that happen during warmup show big jumps. Also check /etc/resolve and whether the instance resolver points to the nated on-prem resolver.
[05:36] Marta (Aurora): we did see a 200ms spike corresponding with resolver queries hitting our on-prem DNS for SAML endpoints. could be correlated.
[05:46] Priya (SE): ok. moving onto KV cache: in our runtime the prefix cache is in-memory on the infer node but for cold restarts it warms from a redis layer. If you have many short-lived connections due to nat port churn, we may not reuse connections to the cache and will do repeated connects, adding ~12-30ms per miss.
[06:08] Alex (AE): does your bench open a fresh connection per request?
[06:13] Leah (Aurora): the client uses a pool but with scaling events a lot of connections were recreated.
[06:19] Priya (SE): that could explain why spike windows align with autoscale events; newly provisioned nodes haven't warmed KV cache. also, quantization: if you configured aggressive 4-bit quant and runtime falls back to 8-bit for some ops, that can trigger a different kernel path which cold-loads small shared objects.
[06:38] Jamal (Aurora): are there debug flags we can turn on that add minimal overhead but show cold cache misses?
[06:44] Priya (SE): yes - we have a lightweight kv-instrument flag that logs miss ratios and connection latencies. i'll send the command.
[06:51] Hank (SE): also enable runtime tracing for model load times (-trace-model-load) for one bench to capture the quantized weight mmap times.
[07:02] Alex (AE): perfect. quick check — anyone seen MTU mismatch manifest as intermittent slow packets rather than consistent drops?
[07:11] Hank (SE): yes, if fragmentation first packet gets through then subsequent larger buffers can hang until retransmit, looks intermittent.
[07:19] Samir (Security): small caution - if you capture pcaps please sanitize IPs and remove patient-data fields, we'll only look at headers.
[07:29] Marta (Aurora): of course.
[07:33] Priya (SE): let's run a coordinated bench: step 1 toggle NAT source/destination check for ENIs to test hairpin, step 2 run with increased ephemeral ports and tcp_tw_recycle / reuse flags adjusted, step 3 run with local resolver pinned to amazon provided resolver to eliminate on-prem resolver, step 4 run with kv instrumentation and runtime trace.
[07:58] Jamal (Aurora): how will PrivateLink change if we go from cross-account to same-account endpoint? will that reduce AZ hops?
[08:06] Priya (SE): potentially — within same account we can pin endpoints closer and the interface ENIs may be in same AZ as your nat gateway; cross-account often forces placement decisions that are less optimal. Also cross-account endpoints are fronted by a different infra that can add NAT steps.
[08:24] Alex (AE): can you describe the current route table setup for the subnet that originates the requests?
[08:30] Leah (Aurora): sure - route table A in private-subnet-1 points to nat-gw-1 in 1a, private-subnet-2 to nat-gw-2 in 1b. private link ENIs are created in 1a and 1b but occasionally traffic hops across, probably because client ENIs prefer one az and nat prefers another.
[08:50] Priya (SE): got it. small misalignments there can cause cross-AZ pathing. For a controlled bench we recommend pinning both client subnets and nat to same AZ to see if tail drops.
[09:03] Jamal (Aurora): ok we'll try AZ pinning.
[09:08] Marta (Aurora): one more thought — we saw increased CPU steal on the appliance during spikes; could be garbage collection on the appliance adding 50ms.
[09:18] Hank (SE): that matches the packet buffer backlog theory. Appliances that buffer for inspection will spike under load.
[09:26] Priya (SE): aside from network, let's talk about batching settings. you said you used 16-way, did you tune max latency windows?
[09:33] Marta (Aurora): default max latency is 150ms in our client library, which means it will wait up to that if not full. we also set a preferred batch size of 12.
[09:43] Priya (SE): ok queueing window of 150ms means if a packet hits a network stall it can balloon. For tight SLOs reduce batch window or enable early flush on egress jitter. Also consider adaptive batching that drops to smaller packs when network RTT variance increases.
[10:01] Alex (AE): any tradeoff in cost when reducing batch size?
[10:04] Priya (SE): throughput will reduce and p50 will stay similar but p99 improves; cost per token might go up slightly since you lose batch efficiency. Redwood Optimize can simulate cost impact — we can run a tradeoff model.
[10:17] Jamal (Aurora): what about quantization? we tried 4-bit and saw some inconsistent quality; sometimes runtime picked fallback kernels during certain attention sizes.
[10:27] Priya (SE): quantization tradeoffs: lower bitwidth reduces memory and throughput per GPU but increases fragility for some ops and can trigger fallback code paths. For production we recommend a validated quant profile per model and a canary phase. If fallback occurs, we have flags to force pre-loading of alternate kernels at startup to avoid cold-path penalty.
[10:51] Marta (Aurora): is that a significant startup hit?
[10:54] Priya (SE): can be 50-120ms once during startup as shared objects are mapped, but it's a one-time cost per process. If you're autoscaling frequently that shows up more.
[11:05] Leah (Aurora): autoscaling frequency — we scale aggressively on CPU usage; maybe we should instead warm nodes during predictable windows.
[11:12] Alex (AE): warming strategy could help; keep a small warm pool so KV cache stays hot. That's part of dedicated capacity benefits.
[11:20] Jamal (Aurora): ok that makes sense.
[11:25] Priya (SE): let's capture an experiment plan here: a) bench with warm pool pinned and KV warmed, b) bench with cold-starts and measure distribution, c) bench with NAT pinned same AZ and resolver pinned. We'll compare p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
[11:44] Marta (Aurora): agreed. can Redwood provide a script that toggles batch window and logs queue times?
[11:50] Priya (SE): yes, small python harness we use for internal perf tests. i'll attach in follow up.
[11:56] Alex (AE): i'll also send a reference config for MTU checks and traceroute instructions.
[12:01] Jamal (Aurora): one oddity — during one run we saw a 900ms outlier; it matched a sequence where kv redis rebalanced and we had a GC on the redis node. worth checking if your cache tier had a maintenance event.
[12:12] Priya (SE): that'll do it; multi-tier dependencies can amplify. We'll ask for a redis timeline too.
[12:20] Hank (SE): i'll add a small header to requests to capture which path they took (X-AZ, X-ENI) to correlate with ENI placement. minimal overhead.
[12:30] Samir (Security): one security note: if we enable additional headers we must strip them before logs persist to avoid leaking internal topology.
[12:38] Priya (SE): agreed.
[12:41] Alex (AE): any other questions on the plan?
[12:45] Jamal (Aurora): timeline looks good. we'll run initial traces this week and upload sanitized pcaps + resolver logs.
[12:52] Marta (Aurora): and we'll try pinning AZ and bump ephemeral port range as suggested.
[12:58] Priya (SE): also check kernel tcp_retries2 and net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout values on the appliance and nat instances. those influence retransmit behavior.
[13:09] Leah (Aurora): noted.
[13:12] Priya (SE): ok closing remarks: likely cause is compound — NAT hairpin + AZ skew + KV cold misses + occasional quant fallback. No single root cause yet but we have a falsification plan.
[13:24] Alex (AE): thanks folks. i'll summarize next steps in the notes.
[13:28] Jamal (Aurora): thanks everyone.
[13:31] Marta (Aurora): thanks.
